# Protocol — local PR CI

Normative protocol for `local/bin/ci.sh`, the local replacement for
`.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml` (frozen under `.github/`, never executed here).
Read `meta.md` first; `build-cache.md` owns the hot-main cache this protocol
consumes but never writes.

`ci.sh <pr-number>` is the **only** thing allowed to publish the `local-ci/*`
commit statuses. Everything downstream — `review.sh` (invariant 2: review only
after green CI on the same head SHA), `autofix.sh` (invariant 3: sync/audit
failures are never auto-fixed), and the merge gate in `pr_merge.py` — reads
those exact-head statuses and the manifest comment this script publishes
(`local/protocols/issues-prs.md` §2), and nothing else.

## 1. What it is

The parent repository consolidated seven workflows into one so that a pull
request produces exactly **one** CI completion event, which the auto-fix
dispatcher keys off (`pr-ci.yml:3-8`). The local port keeps that property: one
invocation, one manifest, one exit code.

```
local/bin/ci.sh <pr-id> [--worktree PATH] [--base REF] [--only STEP]
                        [--force-all] [--skip-build] [--dry-run]
```

`<pr-id>` is the GitHub PR number; the script reads `branch`, `base` and the
head SHA from GitHub (`gh_common.py pr-view`), finds the branch's worktree (via
`git worktree list`, falling back to `.worktrees/<branch with / → ->`), and
runs everything **inside that worktree**. Nothing is run in the primary
checkout, and the worktree's branch tip must equal the remote head before the
run starts.

Exit status: `0` all gating steps passed or were legitimately skipped; `1` at
least one gating step failed or could not run; `2` the run could not start
(unknown PR number, missing worktree, unresolvable base, GitHub unreachable —
a GitHub error never degrades to a local record).

### Preconditions that are hard errors, never silent skips

| Precondition | Why it is fatal |
|---|---|
| GitHub returns an open PR with a head branch | there is no branch to test |
| a worktree for that branch exists | CI must not test the primary checkout |
| `origin/<base>` or `<base>` resolves | invariant 8 — the diff-based audits and the change gating self-disable without a base, which is exactly the "checks silently stopped running" failure the parent repo patched twice |
| a merge base exists | the change set is undefined without one |
| `python3` on `PATH` | every audit job and the manifest writer need it |

There is deliberately **no `LOCAL_CI_ENABLED` kill switch**. `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED`
and `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` exist because a disabled reviewer or fixer merely
stops work from happening; a disabled CI would hand the merge gate a green
light it never earned. If CI must not run, do not run it — the head SHA simply
keeps whatever statuses it already carries.

## 2. Job table

Eight steps, in this order, named exactly after the parent workflow's job ids
so the auto-fix dispatcher's mapping (build → ci-fix, blueprint-render →
blueprint-fix, everything else → never auto-fixed) ports without translation.

| Step | Parent job | What it runs (in the worktree) | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| `build` | `build` (`pr-ci.yml:115-168`) | warm `.lake/build`, `lake exe cache get`, `lake build`, `lake build MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.AxiomAudit` (`:155-156`), `scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py` (`:158-159`) | `lean ∨ comparator ∨ workflow` |
| `blueprint-render` | `blueprint-render` (`:173-243`) | remove the prior PDF, run the project `latexmk` configuration noninteractively, require its exit zero and a fresh non-empty `blueprint/print/print.pdf` (`:210-218`), `texra-blueprint bbl` (`:222-223`), `texra-blueprint web` with `grep '^ERROR:'` (`:225-243`) | `blueprint_src ∨ workflow` |
| `paper-gaps` | `paper-gaps` (`:248-271`) | `texra-blueprint --root . paper-gaps check` | `paper_gaps ∨ workflow` |
| `blueprint-sync` | `blueprint-sync` (`:273-317`) | `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`, `blueprint_lean_sync.py --update-lean-decls`, `blueprint_lean_sync.py --ci`, `blueprint_axiom_audit_needed.py --base-ref` | `lean ∨ blueprint ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |
| `file-length` | `file-length` (`:319-340`) | `check_oversized_lean_files.py --root .` (>1000 lines) | `mip_lean ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |
| `proof-debt` | `proof-debt` (`:342-386`) | `unittest test_audit_paper_facing_proof_debt.py`, `audit_paper_facing_proof_debt.py --ci` | `mip_lean ∨ tex_chapter ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |
| `proof-evasion` | `proof-evasion` (`:388-445`) | four regression tests, then `audit_lean_axiom_declarations.py --ci`, `audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses.py --ci`, `audit_unfaithful_markers.py --ci`, and `check_duplicate_private_helpers.py --ci` (advisory) | `mip_lean ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |
| `statement-origin` | `statement-origin` (`:447-487`) | `check_statement_paper_origin.py --root .` | `ldt_lean ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |

Every step is blocking. The single advisory sub-check is
`check_duplicate_private_helpers.py`: exit 1 means "candidates reported" and is
downgraded to a warning, any other nonzero status is a real failure — the same
`set +e` dance as `pr-ci.yml:432-445`.

The PDF subpass invokes `latexmk` from `blueprint/src`, so the checked status is
the compiler driver's status rather than a wrapper's. It uses the checked-in
`latexmkrc` and adds `nonstopmode`, `halt-on-error`, and file-line diagnostics.
The command must return zero and create a non-empty `print.pdf` after the prior
artifact was removed. A fresh but partial PDF cannot replace a successful
compiler exit. The driver checks that status explicitly because the step
dispatcher disables `errexit` while capturing each outcome; later successful
bbl or web commands must never overwrite an earlier PDF failure.

Two GitHub-only behaviours are dropped on purpose: `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`
blocks and `::error` / `::notice` / `::warning` annotations are inert outside
Actions, so the step's stdout+stderr log **is** the summary. `--github-annotations`
is not passed to `check_duplicate_private_helpers.py`. Exit-code semantics are
preserved exactly: `::warning` never failed a job, and the `^ERROR:` grep
always did.

### Steps that did not run

A step whose area did not change is recorded `skipped` with the reason — never
omitted. A skipped step is green for the merge gate, exactly as a skipped
GitHub job is. This is why the gating globs are load-bearing (§3): a glob that
under-matches turns a real gate into a permanent, invisible `skipped`.

## 3. Gating globs — keep in lockstep

`git diff --name-only --no-renames <merge-base> <head>` replaces
`dorny/paths-filter@v3`. `--no-renames` is deliberate: reporting both the old
and the new path means a rename *out of* a gated tree still trips that tree's
filter, and deletions count. `*` in these patterns spans `/`, matching
minimatch's `**`.

| Area | Globs | Parent |

| `lean` | `*.lean`, `lakefile.*`, `lean-toolchain`, `lake-manifest.json` | `pr-ci.yml:84-88` |
| `mip_lean` | `MIPStarRE/*.lean` | `:89-90` |

> **Lockstep warning.** These globs must move together with the trees the audit
> scripts actually scan. The parent repo patched the `paper_gaps` filter twice

The `workflow` area is the one deliberate extension. On GitHub it meant "the
workflow file changed, so re-run everything"; locally the workflow layer is a
whole tree — the frozen reference `pr-ci.yml`, every driver and helper under

included. The globs are that broad on purpose: a `gh_common.py`-only change has
to run the `scripts/tests` unit suite that covers it — carried by
`blueprint-sync` — and under the old three-file glob such a change matched no
area and ran nothing at all (PR 7 review, F13).

## 4. Manifest schema

Built in runtime storage (same-directory tempfile + `os.replace`) and then
posted as the manifest PR comment (§5):

```
~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.json          complete run
~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.partial.json  partial run
```

A run is **partial** when it was given `--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`;
`--dry-run` writes nothing at all.

Step logs live outside the repository, under
`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/<pr-id>/<head_sha>/<step>.log`.

```jsonc
{
  "schema": 1,
  "generator": "local/bin/ci.sh",
  "replaces": ".github/workflows/pr-ci.yml",
  "pr": 7,                       // GitHub PR number
  "branch": "issue-7-qpbt-basis",
  "base": "main",                // from the GitHub PR
  "base_ref": "origin/main",     // what actually resolved
  "merge_base": "<sha>",
  "head_sha": "<sha>",           // the SHA every step ran against
  "worktree": "/abs/path",
  "started": "2026-08-30T09:23:07+0800",   // ISO-8601 with offset
  "finished": "2026-08-30T09:41:52+0800",
  "seconds": 1125,               // whole run, integer
  "conclusion": "success",       // success | failure | error
  "partial": false,              // true ⇒ not a merge-gate verdict
  "areas": { "lean": true, "blueprint_src": false, ... },
  "changed_files": ["MIPStarRE/Quantum/PauliBasis.lean", ...],
  "warnings": ["texra-blueprint not installed; skipped ...", ...],
  "steps": [
    {
      "step": "build",           // one of the eight job ids, always all eight
      "outcome": "success",      // success | failure | error | skipped
      "seconds": 883,
      "log_path": "/Users/…/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/0007/<sha>/build.log",
      "blocking": true,
      "note": ""                 // skip reason, exit code, or degradation cause
    }
  ]
}
```

Outcome vocabulary — the distinction is what routes the auto-fix loop:

| `outcome` | Meaning | Auto-fix |
|---|---|---|
| `success` | the step ran and passed | — |
| `failure` | the step ran and the code is wrong | `build` → ci-fix, `blueprint-render` → blueprint-fix, everything else → **never** |
| `error` | the step could not run (missing tool, unbootstrapped worktree, build lock unavailable) | never — this is an operator problem, not a code problem |
| `skipped` | gated out, or excluded by `--only` / `--skip-build` | — |

`conclusion` is `failure` if any step failed, else `error` if any step errored,
else `success`. The run's exit status is `0` iff `conclusion == "success"`.

## 5. Publication

Evidence goes to GitHub, bound to the exact SHA the steps ran against
(`issues-prs.md` §2). For every complete run:

* one `local-ci/<step>` status per gate step — `pending` posted before the
  step, then `success | failure | error`; a gated-out step is a `success`
  whose description says it was skipped, so the gate never has to distinguish
  "absent" from "not applicable";
* `local-ci/summary` carrying the run's `conclusion`;
* the manifest JSON as the PR comment marked
  `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, created or updated in place.

`pending` before the first step is the old `ci_status: running`: a crashed,
killed or power-cut run leaves `pending`, never a stale `success`, so the
review gate's "green CI on the same head SHA" check (invariant 2) fails closed.
Immediately before the final publication `ci.sh` re-reads both the local branch
tip and the remote PR head; if either moved, it publishes no success and exits
nonzero, because a status is a claim about one commit.

A **partial** run (`--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`) publishes nothing at
all — no statuses, no manifest comment — and keeps its manifest in runtime
storage only. `--base` belongs on that list because an overridden base (the PR
head, say) can empty the diff and mark every gate skipped-success. Partial runs
are a debugging aid; they must not be able to produce a merge-gate verdict, and
they must not clobber a complete manifest for the same SHA.

## 6. Concurrency and locks

Two advisory `mkdir`-based lease directories, both under
`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/` (`MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT` overrides the root). Each
holds an `owner` file: pid, ISO timestamp, tag. A lock is broken only when its
owner pid is dead or its stamp is older than `MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK_STALE_S`
(default 3 h).

| Lock | Scope | On contention |
|---|---|---|
| `locks/ci-<pr-id>.lock` | one `ci.sh` per PR | **refuse immediately** (exit 2) |
| `$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock` | one full `lake build` machine-wide (invariant 7) | wait up to `MIPSTARRE_CI_BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S` (default 4 h), then record `build` as `error` and continue with the Python steps |

Only the `build` step takes the full-build lock. The audits are pure Python and
take nothing; single-file `lake env lean` checks are read-only over oleans and
take nothing either — which is precisely why `.githooks/pre-push` can use them
per-file without serializing.

`ci.sh` never cancels a running build. GitHub cancels in-progress PR runs
(`pr-ci.yml:48-51`) because its runners are disposable and main-branch runs —
the ones that seed the cache — are exempt. Locally there is nothing disposable:
killing a build mid-flight leaves a half-written `.lake/build` and a held lease.
So a second run for the same PR is refused, and a foreign live build lease is
waited on, never stolen. Do not `kill -9` a running `ci.sh`; if you must, remove
the lease directories by hand.

## 7. Build step and the two-tier cache

`build` is the only step that touches the cache, and it only ever **reads** the
shared tree. This is the local translation of the parent's main-only cache save
policy, whose rationale is documented at `pr-ci.yml:137-142`: per-PR saves of
~2.6 GB cycled through the 10 GB repository budget and evicted the main entry,
so no run ever restored usable oleans. The local failure mode is identical if a
worktree writes into the shared snapshot, so it does not.

1. If `.lake/build` is absent, run `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh <worktree>`,
   which resolves the hot-main snapshot and clones it copy-on-write. Contract:
   idempotent, exit 0 when it populated or deliberately declined, nonzero on a
   hard error.
   - warmer missing → loud warning, cold build (still correct, just slow);
     set `MIPSTARRE_CI_REQUIRE_WARMER=1` to make it an `error` instead.
2. `.lake/build` (this project's oleans, per-worktree, writable) and
   `.lake/packages` (Mathlib and friends) are **different tiers** and are never
   conflated. If `.lake/packages` is a symlink it points at the shared hot-main
   dependency tree and is read-only: `lake exe cache get` is **skipped**,
   because it writes there. If it is a real directory, `lake exe cache get`
   runs, mirroring what `lean-action` does inside the parent job. Never run
   `lake update` in a consumer worktree.
3. `.lake/packages` absent entirely → `error`, pointing at
   `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh`. That bootstrap path is where the ProofWidgets
   prune workaround lives, and a package-free tree is exactly the state that
   triggers it. `MIPSTARRE_CI_ALLOW_COLD_FETCH=1` overrides for a tree you know
   is clean.
4. `lake build`, then `lake build MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.AxiomAudit`,
   then the comparator drift check.  Both audit modules are compile-time
   checks, not reports: each `audit_standard_axioms` /
   `assert_standard_axioms` command calls `Lean.collectAxioms` and throws
   unless the declaration's axioms are exactly `propext`,
   `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`, so a `sorryAx` reaching a headline
   theorem fails the build step.  They are built as explicit targets
   rather than imported from the umbrella libraries, so they stay out of
   normal downstream imports.

For reviewed trains, `--integration-head SHA --worktree PATH --base SHA` runs
every step without publishing PR evidence. Its single locked Lake invocation is
`lake build MIPStarRE MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.AxiomAudit`:
the complete library, including its root and downstream modules, plus both
axiom audits. No warm project
artifacts may be assumed by publication's dynamic `checkdecls` import. Skip flags
are rejected; the exact head, base ancestry, and clean worktree are checked.

Every `lake` and `python3` invocation goes through a subshell that unsets
`git rev-parse --local-env-vars` first. Inherited `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE`
make Lake resolve nested package repositories against the wrong repository;

# Canonical-complement source integration

## Source and Scope

The source is Definition `def:canonical-complement` and its following remarks
in `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:303-340`, with the ambient
finite-field convention at lines 219-222. Independent coordinate rows are
reduced by a canonical Gaussian-elimination algorithm valid over arbitrary
fields. The complement consists of the standard basis vectors in the nonpivot
columns. The source explicitly asserts efficient computation, without a
particular arithmetic exponent or an arbitrary-field bit representation.

This author-side integration starts at
`8f55fc058512f43f69c8c869de349613bbf2de59`. It reads and checks the construction
documented in [the algorithm audit](2026-09-22_issue-690-canonical-elimination.md).
It imports `Algebra.RowEchelonAlgorithm` from `MIPStarRE.QPBT`, links its
construction and proofs in chapter 11, and marks the canonical definition.
It changes no algebraic definition, theorem statement, or proof. The preceding
RREF module and all predecessor audits remain intact.

## Construction and Mathematical Correspondence

The program takes a materialized matrix over `Field K`, with `DecidableEq K`.
It scans columns from left to right, searches a bounded list for the first
eligible nonzero row, interchanges that row with the next pivot row, divides
by the nonzero pivot, and clears its column in every other row. The normalized
row and resulting matrix are stored before subsequent use.

The entrywise row formulas in `eliminateColumn_apply` agree with this
description. `eliminateColumn_span` proves both span inclusions by reversing
the row operations. `eliminateColumn_entries` establishes a unit pivot column
and preservation of earlier columns. `findPivot_spec` identifies the search
with the first eligible list element and bounds its charges by the list length.

`Invariant.step` preserves ordered unit pivot columns, leading zeros, zeros
in inspected columns of the remaining rows, and equality of row spans.
`runColumns_invariant` derives this invariant from the input alone.
`gaussianElimination_correct` applies it to the nonzero-row view, proves that
all trailing rows vanish, and identifies the computed nonpivot set with
`canonicalComplement` using the existing RREF correspondence.
`gaussianElimination_of_linearIndependent` uses equality of row-space
dimensions to show that all `m` rows are pivot rows for independent input.
Neither theorem takes a correctness certificate or a complement identity as
an input. The output rows and pivots read the computed storage, rather than
an abstract existence witness.

The source complement is a set of vectors. Lean represents its coordinate
indices by a finite set and its vectors by the corresponding standard basis
vectors. The retained cardinality, independence, basis-independence, and
register-subspace theorems establish the other assertions of the source
definition and remarks.

New algorithm formulas use paper rows `a=1,...,m` and columns `b=1,...,n`.
Their formal indices are `i=a-1` and `j=b-1`, and
`p_paper(a)=p_Lean(a-1)+1`. After `r` completed pivots, paper row `r+1`
has formal index `r`. The new correctness entry explains that the prefix
lengths `b,b-1` become `j+1,j`; it introduces no coordinate sums with an
implicit index conversion.

## Cost Model and Verdict

Each field division, multiplication, subtraction, and equality test has unit
cost. `tabulateCounted` first evaluates each entry computation into a stored
value/count pair, then reads these pairs to extract values and sum their
charges. The normalized pivot row costs `n` divisions. Clearing the remaining
rows costs at most `2*m*n` operations, conservatively including the pivot
row in that upper bound. Every inspected search row costs one test, even when
an index comparison short-circuits the field test. There are at most `m`
inspected rows per column.

The program accumulates those charges as it constructs the matrices.
`gaussianElimination_cost_le_poly` proves the bound
`n*(m+n+m*(2*n))`, arithmetically the displayed `n*(m+n+2*m*n)`.
This is a bound on the actual conservative counter, not an unrelated nominal
counter or a caller-supplied complexity assertion.

The bound starts with stored input. `ofMatrix` tabulates each input entry once;
arbitrary computation within an external entry-producing function is outside
the theorem. Array reads perform no field arithmetic. The code makes bounded
passes of sizes at most `m`, `n`, and `m*n` per column for row search,
tabulation, summation of counts, and pivot updates. The nonpivot selection
performs at most `m*n` comparisons of stored pivot indices. These observations
explain polynomial administrative work in the ordinary array model; there is
no formal instruction-count, memory-allocation, or field-encoding theorem.

The source's arbitrary-field elimination is therefore realized in the
unit-cost arithmetic model. Executable field operations and equality specify
how to run an algorithm over a supplied field; they do not assume the desired
RREF, span, complement, or efficiency conclusion. An unrestricted
representation-uniform bit-complexity statement over arbitrary fields would
require information the source passage does not supply, and is not claimed
here. The source definition receives its mark on this explicit arithmetic
interpretation, with no permanent exemption or altered mathematical domain.

## Statement Integrity

| Aspect | Paper | Linked Lean result | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Field | Finite ambient field; elimination valid over arbitrary fields | `Field K` with supplied operations and `DecidableEq K` | Faithful computational boundary data |
| Dimensions | Finite row family, positive ambient dimension | Natural `m,n`, including zero | Exact on source domain, with degenerate extensions |
| Input | Independent coordinate rows | Stored matrix and `LinearIndependent K (toMatrix A).row` | Same mathematical hypothesis |
| Reduced form | Ordered leading ones with reduced pivot columns | Existing entrywise `IsReducedRowEchelon` on the computed output | Exact |
| Row span | Preserved by elimination | Equality with the input row span, proved internally | Exact |
| Complement | Nonpivot standard basis vectors | Computed nonpivot indices equal the intrinsic complement | Faithful finite-index representation |
| Efficiency | Efficient arbitrary-field Gaussian elimination | Polynomial charged-operation bound for the executable program | Faithful unit-cost arithmetic interpretation |

The overall verdict is **faithful boundary hypotheses**, with no added
mathematical premise and no weakened conclusion. General dependent-row
correctness and zero-dimensional cases extend the source domain. No claim is
made that this closes any unrelated source discrepancy or the QPBT track.

REF 87382b80522b3a859653929ca20ddbc760079a11 challenge_config.py
     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""Per-challenge configuration for the comparator challenge generator.
     3	
     4	A *challenge* is one self-contained `Challenge.lean` file: the Lean modules the
     5	extractor must import, the target theorems whose statement closure it extracts,
     6	the header and footer wrapped around the assembled body, the checked-in
     7	expected copy, and the elaboration-context tables (`extras`,
     8	`module_preludes`) that the kernel closure cannot see.
     9	
    10	Configurations live in `scripts/comparator/challenges/<name>.json` and are read
    11	by `extract_closure.lean` (through the environment), `assemble_challenge.py`
    12	and `check_challenge_drift.py`.  See README.md in this directory.
    13	
    14	Schema (unknown top-level keys are rejected so typos fail loudly):
    15	
    16	```jsonc
    17	{
    18	  "name": "ldt",                       // required, must equal the file stem
    19	  "description": "…",                  // optional, free text
    20	  "imports": ["MIPStarRE.…"],          // required, non-empty
    21	  "targets": ["MIPStarRE.…"],          // required, non-empty; closure roots
    22	  "header": "scripts/…/header.lean",   // optional, null to omit
    23	  "footer": "scripts/…/footer.lean",   // optional, null to omit
    24	  "expected": "scripts/…/Challenge.lean.expected",   // required
    25	  "require_expected": true,            // optional, default true
    26	  "split": false,                      // optional, default false
    27	  "common_opens": ["open scoped …"],  // optional, split-module context
    28	  "extras": {"Decl.Name": ["line"]},   // optional
    29	  "module_preludes": {                 // optional
    30	    // one scope covering the whole module …
    31	    "MIPStarRE/…/Module.lean": {"namespace": ["A", "B"], "lines": ["open …"]},
    32	    // … or several, each covering a line range of it
    33	    "MIPStarRE/…/Other.lean": [
    34	      {"namespace": ["A"], "lines": ["variable …"], "first": 52, "last": 94},
    35	      {"namespace": ["A"], "lines": ["variable …"], "first": 96, "last": 223,
    36	       "noncomputable": true}
    37	    ]
    38	  }
    39	}
    40	```
    41	
    42	A module needs one scope per source section whose elaboration context differs:
    43	the self-dual normal basis file, for instance, has a group-algebra section and
    44	a trace-dual section binding the same identifier to different things.  A scope
    45	opened with `noncomputable section` in the source is marked `noncomputable`,
    46	because the definitions inside such a section carry no `noncomputable` keyword
    47	of their own and do not re-elaborate outside one.
    48	"""
    49	
    50	from __future__ import annotations
    51	
    52	import json
    53	import re
    54	from dataclasses import dataclass
    55	from pathlib import Path
    56	from typing import Any
    57	
    58	# Configuration lives next to the scripts that read it, not under the tree
    59	# being checked: `--root` names the library tree, which may be a different
    60	# worktree than the one these scripts were invoked from.
    61	CHALLENGE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "challenges"
    62	DEFAULT_CHALLENGE = "ldt"
    63	
    64	# Read by `extract_closure.lean`; comma-separated fully qualified names.
    65	TARGETS_ENV = "MIPSTARRE_COMPARATOR_TARGETS"
    66	
    67	# `last` of a scope that runs to the end of its module
    68	LAST_LINE = 10**9
    69	
    70	_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*\Z")
    71	
    72	_KEYS = {
    73	    "name",
    74	    "description",
    75	    "imports",
    76	    "targets",
    77	    "header",
    78	    "footer",
    79	    "expected",
    80	    "require_expected",
    81	    "split",
    82	    "common_opens",
    83	    "extras",
    84	    "module_preludes",
    85	}
    86	
    87	_PRELUDE_KEYS = {"namespace", "lines", "first", "last", "noncomputable"}
    88	
    89	
    90	class ChallengeConfigError(ValueError):
    91	    """A challenge configuration is missing a key, or a key has a wrong type."""
    92	
    93	
    94	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    95	class Prelude:
    96	    """Elaboration context of one source scope of one module.
    97	
    98	    The `open`s, `variable`s and `local notation` that the declarations of a
    99	    source section were elaborated under, replayed around the snippets taken
   100	    from lines `first`..`last` of that module.
   101	    """
   102	
   103	    namespace: tuple[str, ...]
   104	    lines: tuple[str, ...]
   105	    first: int = 1
   106	    last: int = LAST_LINE
   107	    noncomputable: bool = False

   230	def _module_preludes(data: dict[str, Any], where: Path) -> dict[str, tuple[Prelude, ...]]:
   231	    raw = data.get("module_preludes", {})
   232	    if not isinstance(raw, dict):

   234	    table: dict[str, tuple[Prelude, ...]] = {}

   237	        scopes = tuple(_prelude(item, module, where) for item in entries)

    82	def tree_diff(expected: dict[str, bytes], candidate: dict[str, bytes]) -> str:
    83	    out: list[str] = []
    84	    for rel in sorted(set(expected) | set(candidate)):
    85	        old_bytes = expected.get(rel)
    86	        new_bytes = candidate.get(rel)
    87	        if old_bytes == new_bytes:
    88	            continue
    89	        if old_bytes is None:
    90	            out.append(f"--- missing from the checked-in copy: {rel}\n")
    91	            continue
    92	        if new_bytes is None:
    93	            out.append(f"--- no longer generated: {rel}\n")
    94	            continue
    95	        out.extend(
    96	            difflib.unified_diff(
    97	                old_bytes.decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines(True),
    98	                new_bytes.decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines(True),
    99	                fromfile=f"checked-in {rel}",
   100	                tofile=f"regenerated {rel}",
   101	            )
   102	        )
   103	    return "".join(out)

   511	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   512	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   513	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   514	  let basis := (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   515	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   516	    ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.variable 0),
   517	      Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.variable 4)} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   518	  let pairs := (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image fun W =>
   519	    Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair
   520	  let magic := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 6 × Fin 3)).image fun ij =>
   521	    Sym2.mk (.constraint ij.1) (.variable (magicVariable ij.1 ij.2))
   522	  loops ∪ lines ∪ basis ∪ pairs ∪ magic
   523	/-- The ordered carrier of the Pauli type graph. -/
   524	abbrev PauliEdge :=
   525	  {e : PauliType × PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ pauliEdges}
   526	/-- A loop supplies the nonempty ordered-edge carrier. -/
   527	instance : Nonempty PauliEdge :=
   528	  ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), by simp [pauliEdges]⟩⟩
   529	/-- A typed Pauli question, retaining every ambient coordinate. -/
   530	abbrev PauliQuestion (P : PauliParams) (K : Type) := PauliType × PauliSpace P K
   531	/-- Full finite question coordinates have decidable equality. -/
   532	noncomputable instance {P : PauliParams} {K : Type} [DecidableEq K] :
   533	    DecidableEq (PauliQuestion P K) := Classical.decEq _
   534	/-- The question law is uniform on all ordered edges and the full seed space. -/
   535	noncomputable def pauliQuestionPMF {K : Type} [Field K] [Fintype K]
   536	    [DecidableEq K] (P : PauliParams) (encoding : K ≃ Fin P.q) :
   537	    PMF (PauliQuestion P K × PauliQuestion P K) :=
   538	  (PMF.uniformOfFintype (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P K)).map fun s =>
   539	    ((s.1.1.1, pauliMap P encoding s.1.1.1 s.2),
   540	      (s.1.1.2, pauliMap P encoding s.1.1.2 s.2))
   541	/-- The seven answer forms, including malformed answers at every question. -/
   542	inductive PauliAnswer (P : PauliParams) (K : Type) where
   543	  | value (a : K)
   544	  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → K)
   545	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → K)
   546	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   547	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
   548	  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
   549	  | pauliOutcome (a : (Fin P.m → Bool) → K)
   550	  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
   551	/-- Whether an answer constructor is prescribed by its question type. -/
   552	def validPauliAnswer {P : PauliParams} {K : Type} :
   553	    PauliType → PauliAnswer P K → Bool
   554	  | .point _, .value _ | .aline _, .alinePoly _ | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true
   555	  | .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ | .pairW _, .bit _ | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
   556	  | .constraint _, .msTriple _ | .variable _, .bit _ => true
   557	  | _, _ => false
   558	/-- One entry of the Boolean-cube indicator vector. -/
   559	def pauliIndicator {P : PauliParams} {K : Type} [CommRing K]
   560	    (x : Fin P.m → K) (y : Fin P.m → Bool) : K :=
   561	  ∏ i : Fin P.m, if y i then x i else 1 - x i
   562	/-- Evaluate the multilinear low-degree encoding of a Pauli outcome. -/
   563	def pauliEncoded {P : PauliParams} {K : Type} [CommRing K]
   564	    (h : (Fin P.m → Bool) → K) (x : Fin P.m → K) : K :=
   565	  dotProduct h (pauliIndicator x)
   566	/-- The phase bit computed from the shared tuple coordinates. -/
   567	def pauliGamma {P : PauliParams} {K : Type} [CommRing K]
   568	    (trace : K → ZMod 2) (z : PauliSpace P K) : ZMod 2 :=
   569	  trace (dotProduct (z.2.2.2.2.1 • pauliIndicator z.1)
   570	    (z.2.2.2.2.2 • pauliIndicator z.2.1))
   571	/-- The complete Pauli verifier, including gamma gates and off-edge defaults. -/
   572	noncomputable def pauliWin {K : Type} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   573	    (P : PauliParams) (encoding : K ≃ Fin P.q) (trace : K → ZMod 2) :
   574	    PauliQuestion P K → PauliQuestion P K → PauliAnswer P K → PauliAnswer P K → Bool :=
   575	  open Classical in
   576	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   577	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   578	      if tA = tB then decide (a = b) else
   579	      match tA, tB, a, b with
   580	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u => if W = W' then decide (∀ t,
   581	          pauliPointBlock W xB = pauliPointBlock W xA +
   582	            t • Pi.single (pauliChiIndex P encoding xA.2.2.1) 1 →
   583	          lowDegreeEval f t = u) else true
   584	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f => if W = W' then decide (∀ t,
   585	          pauliPointBlock W xA = pauliPointBlock W xB +
   586	            t • Pi.single (pauliChiIndex P encoding xB.2.2.1) 1 →
   587	          lowDegreeEval f t = u) else true
   588	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u => if W = W' then decide (∀ t,
   589	          pauliPointBlock W xB = pauliPointBlock W xA + t • xA.2.2.2.1 →
   590	          lowDegreeEval f t = u) else true
   591	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f => if W = W' then decide (∀ t,
   592	          pauliPointBlock W xA = pauliPointBlock W xB + t • xB.2.2.2.1 →
   593	          lowDegreeEval f t = u) else true
   594	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   595	          if W = W' then decide (pauliEncoded h (pauliPointBlock W xA) = u) else true
   596	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   597	          if W = W' then decide (pauliEncoded h (pauliPointBlock W xB) = u) else true
   598	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits => decide (pauliGamma trace xA ≠ 0 ∨
   599	          match W with | .X => bits.1 = β | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   600	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β => decide (pauliGamma trace xB ≠ 0 ∨
   601	          match W with | .X => bits.1 = β | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   602	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β => if W = W' then decide
   603	          (pauliGamma trace xB ≠ 0 ∨ trace (u * if W = .X then xB.2.2.2.2.1
   604	            else xB.2.2.2.2.2) = β) else true
   605	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u => if W = W' then decide
   606	          (pauliGamma trace xA ≠ 0 ∨ trace (u * if W = .X then xA.2.2.2.2.1
   607	            else xA.2.2.2.2.2) = β) else true
   608	      | .constraint i, .variable j, .msTriple bits, .bit β =>
   609	          if ∃ k, magicVariable i k = j then decide (pauliGamma trace xA = 0 ∨
   610	            (∑ k, bits k) = magicParity i ∧ ∃ k, magicVariable i k = j ∧ bits k = β)
   611	          else true
   612	      | .variable j, .constraint i, .bit β, .msTriple bits =>
   613	          if ∃ k, magicVariable i k = j then decide (pauliGamma trace xB = 0 ∨
   614	            (∑ k, bits k) = magicParity i ∧ ∃ k, magicVariable i k = j ∧ bits k = β)
   615	          else true
   616	      | .point W, .variable j, .value u, .bit β => decide (pauliGamma trace xB = 0 ∨
   617	          (j = 0 ∧ W = .X ∧ trace (u * xB.2.2.2.2.1) = β) ∨
   618	          (j = 4 ∧ W = .Z ∧ trace (u * xB.2.2.2.2.2) = β))
   619	      | .variable j, .point W, .bit β, .value u => decide (pauliGamma trace xA = 0 ∨
   620	          (j = 0 ∧ W = .X ∧ trace (u * xA.2.2.2.2.1) = β) ∨
   621	          (j = 4 ∧ W = .Z ∧ trace (u * xA.2.2.2.2.2) = β))
   622	      | _, _, _, _ => true
   623	    else false
   624	/-- The compact Pauli basis game. -/
   625	noncomputable def pauliGame {K : Type} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   626	    (P : PauliParams) (encoding : K ≃ Fin P.q) (trace : K → ZMod 2) :
   627	    Game (PauliQuestion P K) (PauliQuestion P K) (PauliAnswer P K) (PauliAnswer P K) := by
   628	  classical
   629	  exact { μ := pauliQuestionPMF P encoding, decide := pauliWin P encoding trace }
   630	/-- A compact strategy on the full Pauli question and answer carriers. -/
   631	abbrev PauliStrategy (P : PauliParams) (K : Type) [Fintype K] :=
   632	  Strategy (PauliQuestion P K) (PauliQuestion P K)
   633	    (PauliAnswer P K) (PauliAnswer P K)
   634	/-- A compact symmetric strategy on the full Pauli carriers. -/
   635	abbrev SymmetricPauliStrategy (P : PauliParams) (K : Type) [Fintype K] :=
   636	  SymmetricStrategy (PauliQuestion P K) (PauliAnswer P K)
   637	/-- The field-valued Boolean-cube register in the Pauli soundness conclusion. -/
   638	abbrev PauliRegister (P : PauliParams) (K : Type) :=
   639	  (Fin P.m → Bool) → K
   640	/-- The binary register obtained by expanding each field coordinate in a fixed basis. -/
   641	abbrev QubitRegister (P : PauliParams) (r : ℕ) :=
   642	  (Fin P.m → Bool) × Fin r → ZMod 2
   643	/-- The prescribed Pauli-basis question with zero ambient seed. -/
   644	def pauliMeasurementQuestion {K : Type} [Zero K]
   645	    (P : PauliParams) (W : PauliKind) : PauliQuestion P K :=
   646	  (.pauli W, 0)
   647	/-- The concrete projective, consistent, support-wise commuting predicate for
   648	the compact Pauli question law. -/
   649	def SymmetricStrategy.IsPauliSPCC {K : Type} [Field K] [Fintype K]
   650	    [DecidableEq K] (P : PauliParams) (encoding : K ≃ Fin P.q)
   651	    (S : SymmetricPauliStrategy P K) : Prop :=
   652	  (∀ x, (S.meas x).IsProjective) ∧ S.IsConsistent ∧
   653	    IsCommutingOn (pauliQuestionPMF P encoding) S.meas S.meas
   654	/-- The error scale in the Pauli soundness and qubit-soundness conclusions. -/
   655	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b epsilon : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   656	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
   657	    (Real.rpow epsilon b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
   658	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
   659	/-- The sign character used in the characteristic-two Pauli eigenvectors. -/
   660	noncomputable def pauliPhaseSign (t : ZMod 2) : ℂ :=
   661	  if t = 0 then 1 else -1
   662	/-- One coordinate of a generalized Pauli eigenvector. -/
   663	noncomputable def singlePauliVec {K : Type} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   664	    (trace : K → ZMod 2) (W : PauliKind) (e x : K) : ℂ :=
   665	  match W with
   666	  | .Z => if x = e then 1 else 0
   667	  | .X =>
   668	      (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ * pauliPhaseSign (trace (e * x))
   669	/-- The tensor-product generalized Pauli eigenvector. -/
   670	noncomputable def pauliVec {K I : Type} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   671	    [Fintype I] (trace : K → ZMod 2) (W : PauliKind)
   672	    (e x : I → K) : ℂ :=
   673	  ∏ i : I, singlePauliVec trace W (e i) (x i)
   674	/-- The rank-one generalized Pauli projector. -/
   675	noncomputable def pauliProj {K I : Type} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   676	    [Fintype I] (trace : K → ZMod 2) (W : PauliKind)
   677	    (e : I → K) : Matrix (I → K) (I → K) ℂ :=
   678	  Matrix.vecMulVec (pauliVec trace W e) (fun x => star (pauliVec trace W e x))
   679	/-- The binary Pauli projector, using the trace of `ZMod 2` over itself. -/
   680	noncomputable abbrev qubitPauliProj {I : Type} [Fintype I]
   681	    (W : PauliKind) (e : I → ZMod 2) : Matrix (I → ZMod 2) (I → ZMod 2) ℂ :=
   682	  pauliProj (Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) (ZMod 2)) W e
   683	/-- Conjugate an operator by a local linear isometry. -/
   684	noncomputable def conjIsometry {I J : Type} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
   685	    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   686	    (phi : EuclideanSpace ℂ I →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ J)
   687	    (M : Matrix I I ℂ) : Matrix J J ℂ :=
   688	  let U : Matrix J I ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm phi.toLinearMap
   689	  U * M * Uᴴ
   690	/-- Lift Alice's conjugated qudit effect to the full extracted target space. -/
   691	noncomputable def liftedPauliAliceEffect
   692	    {I I' J' R : Type} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
   693	    [Fintype I'] [DecidableEq I'] [Fintype J'] [DecidableEq J']
   694	    [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
   695	    (phi : EuclideanSpace ℂ I →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (I' × R))
   696	    (M : Matrix I I ℂ) :
   697	    Matrix ((I' × R) × (J' × R)) ((I' × R) × (J' × R)) ℂ :=
   698	  fun p q => if p.2 = q.2 then conjIsometry phi M p.1 q.1 else 0
   699	/-- Lift Bob's conjugated qudit effect to the full extracted target space. -/
   700	noncomputable def liftedPauliBobEffect
   701	    {I I' J' R : Type} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
   702	    [Fintype I'] [DecidableEq I'] [Fintype J'] [DecidableEq J']
   703	    [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
   704	    (phi : EuclideanSpace ℂ I →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (J' × R))
   705	    (M : Matrix I I ℂ) :
   706	    Matrix ((I' × R) × (J' × R)) ((I' × R) × (J' × R)) ℂ :=
   707	  fun p q => if p.1 = q.1 then conjIsometry phi M p.2 q.2 else 0
   708	/-- Lift Alice's conjugated qubit effect by tensoring with Bob's identity. -/
   709	noncomputable def liftedQubitAliceEffect
   710	    {I I' J' R : Type} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
   711	    [Fintype I'] [DecidableEq I'] [Fintype J'] [DecidableEq J']
   712	    [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
   713	    (phi : EuclideanSpace ℂ I →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (I' × R))
   714	    (M : Matrix I I ℂ) :
   715	    Matrix ((I' × R) × (J' × R)) ((I' × R) × (J' × R)) ℂ :=
   716	  Matrix.kronecker (conjIsometry phi M) 1
   717	/-- Lift Bob's conjugated qubit effect by tensoring with Alice's identity. -/
   718	noncomputable def liftedQubitBobEffect
   719	    {I I' J' R : Type} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
   720	    [Fintype I'] [DecidableEq I'] [Fintype J'] [DecidableEq J']
   721	    [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
   722	    (phi : EuclideanSpace ℂ I →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (J' × R))
   723	    (M : Matrix I I ℂ) :
   724	    Matrix ((I' × R) × (J' × R)) ((I' × R) × (J' × R)) ℂ :=
   725	  Matrix.kronecker 1 (conjIsometry phi M)
   726	/-- Place a register projector on Alice's target register. -/
   727	noncomputable def idealProjectorAlice {I' J' R : Type}
   728	    [DecidableEq I'] [DecidableEq J'] [DecidableEq R]
   729	    (M : Matrix R R ℂ) :
   730	    Matrix ((I' × R) × (J' × R)) ((I' × R) × (J' × R)) ℂ :=
   731	  fun p q => if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then M p.1.2 q.1.2 else 0
   732	/-- Place a register projector on Bob's target register. -/
   733	noncomputable def idealProjectorBob {I' J' R : Type}
   734	    [DecidableEq I'] [DecidableEq J'] [DecidableEq R]
   735	    (M : Matrix R R ℂ) :
   736	    Matrix ((I' × R) × (J' × R)) ((I' × R) × (J' × R)) ℂ :=
   737	  fun p q => if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then M p.2.2 q.2.2 else 0
   738	/-- Expand a field-valued register label in fixed binary coordinates. -/
   739	def binaryRegisterLabel {P : PauliParams} {K : Type} {r : ℕ}
   740	    (coordinates : K → Fin r → ZMod 2) (u : PauliRegister P K) :
   741	    QubitRegister P r :=
   742	  fun p => coordinates (u p.1) p.2
   743	/-- Alice's raw prescribed-answer qudit operator error. -/
   744	noncomputable def rawPauliAliceError {K : Type} [Field K] [Fintype K]
   745	    [DecidableEq K] (P : PauliParams) (S : PauliStrategy P K)
   746	    (w : ExtractionWitness (R := PauliRegister P K) S)
   747	    (trace : K → ZMod 2) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   748	  aliceOperatorError w
   749	    (fun u => liftedPauliAliceEffect (J' := w.ιB') w.φA
   750	      ((S.alice (pauliMeasurementQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)))
   751	    (fun u => idealProjectorAlice (J' := w.ιB') (pauliProj trace W u))
   752	/-- Bob's raw prescribed-answer qudit operator error. -/
   753	noncomputable def rawPauliBobError {K : Type} [Field K] [Fintype K]
   754	    [DecidableEq K] (P : PauliParams) (S : PauliStrategy P K)
   755	    (w : ExtractionWitness (R := PauliRegister P K) S)
   756	    (trace : K → ZMod 2) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   757	  bobOperatorError w
   758	    (fun u => liftedPauliBobEffect (I' := w.ιA') w.φB
   759	      ((S.bob (pauliMeasurementQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)))
   760	    (fun u => idealProjectorBob (I' := w.ιA') (pauliProj trace W u))
   761	/-- Alice's raw prescribed-answer qubit operator error, summed over the
   762	original field-valued outcomes. -/
   763	noncomputable def rawQubitAliceError {K : Type} [Field K] [Fintype K]
   764	    [DecidableEq K] {r : ℕ} (P : PauliParams) (S : PauliStrategy P K)
   765	    (w : ExtractionWitness (R := QubitRegister P r) S)
   766	    (coordinates : K → Fin r → ZMod 2) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   767	  aliceOperatorError w
   768	    (fun u => liftedQubitAliceEffect (J' := w.ιB') w.φA
   769	      ((S.alice (pauliMeasurementQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)))
   770	    (fun u => idealProjectorAlice (J' := w.ιB')
   771	      (qubitPauliProj W (binaryRegisterLabel coordinates u)))
   772	/-- Bob's raw prescribed-answer qubit operator error, summed over the
   773	original field-valued outcomes. -/
   774	noncomputable def rawQubitBobError {K : Type} [Field K] [Fintype K]
   775	    [DecidableEq K] {r : ℕ} (P : PauliParams) (S : PauliStrategy P K)
   776	    (w : ExtractionWitness (R := QubitRegister P r) S)
   777	    (coordinates : K → Fin r → ZMod 2) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   778	  bobOperatorError w
   779	    (fun u => liftedQubitBobEffect (I' := w.ιA') w.φB
   780	      ((S.bob (pauliMeasurementQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)))
   781	    (fun u => idealProjectorBob (I' := w.ιA')
   782	      (qubitPauliProj W (binaryRegisterLabel coordinates u)))

   784	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
   785	/-- `IsAdmissibleSize q` is the predicate `q = 2^k` for an odd exponent.
   786	This is blueprint `def:admissible-size`, with paper origin
   787	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:662-667`.
   788	-/
   789	def IsAdmissibleSize (q : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ k : ℕ, Odd k ∧ q = 2 ^ k
   790	/--
   791	A fixed finite-field model records the carrier and the chosen coding of its
   792	elements by `Fin q`.  The algebra structure and stored basis data make explicit
   793	the paper's once-and-for-all self-dual normal-basis convention; they are
   794	deliberately part of the model rather than quantified afresh by the soundness
   795	theorem.  This is the Lean carrier for blueprint
   796	`def:binary-representation`, paper origin
   797	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-728`.
   798	-/
   799	/- The finite-field carrier is specialized to `Type 0`, as are the finite
   800	models used by the surrounding Euclidean-space API. -/
   801	structure FixedFieldModel (q : ℕ) extends MIPStarRE.LDT.FieldModel.{0} q where
   802	  /-- Scalar restriction from `ZMod 2` to the chosen field. -/
   803	  algebra : Algebra (ZMod 2) K
   804	  /-- Dimension of the chosen basis over the prime subfield. -/
   805	  basisDim : ℕ
   806	  /-- The chosen basis dimension is odd, as required for a self-dual normal basis
   807	  over the binary field. -/
   808	  basisDimOdd : Odd basisDim
   809	  /-- The admissible field-size relation for the chosen basis dimension. -/
   810	  basisCard : q = 2 ^ basisDim
   811	  /-- The chosen basis of `K` over `ZMod 2`. -/
   812	  basis : Module.Basis (Fin basisDim) (ZMod 2) K
   813	  /--
   814	  The inherited coding of `K` is the natural binary encoding of the stored
   815	  basis coordinates.  This field records the source's `downsize` convention
   816	  rather than allowing an unrelated permutation of `Fin q`.  It is the
   817	  coordinate clause of blueprint
   818	  `def:binary-representation`, with paper origin
   819	  `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:669-680`.
   820	  -/
   821	  representation_natural :
   822	    ∀ v : Fin basisDim → ZMod 2,
   823	      (toFieldModel.equiv (basis.equivFun.symm v)).val =
   824	        ∑ i : Fin basisDim, if v i = 1 then 2 ^ i.1 else 0
   825	  /-- Self-duality of the chosen basis with respect to the field trace. -/
   826	  selfDual : ∀ i j, Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K (basis i * basis j) =
   827	    if i = j then 1 else 0
   828	  /-- Normality of the chosen basis, recorded by a Frobenius generator. -/
   829	  normal : ∃ α : K, ∀ i, basis i = α ^ (2 ^ i.1)
   830	/-- The once-and-for-all field model selected for an admissible size.  Every
   831	QPBT parameter record uses this same choice, matching the paper's fixed
   832	self-dual normal-basis identification rather than quantifying over arbitrary
   833	representations.  Blueprint `def:binary-representation`; paper origin
   834	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-680`.
   835	-/
   836	noncomputable def fixedFieldModel (q : ℕ) (hq : IsAdmissibleSize q) :
   837	    FixedFieldModel q := by
   838	  sorry
   839	instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : Field F.K := F.toFieldModel.instField
   840	instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : Fintype F.K := F.toFieldModel.instFintype
   841	instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : DecidableEq F.K := F.toFieldModel.instDecidableEq

    20	/-- A Lean library's declarative configuration. -/
    21	public configuration LeanLibConfig (name : Name) extends LeanConfig where
    22	  /--
    23	  The subdirectory of the package's source directory containing the library's
    24	  Lean source files. Defaults simply to said `srcDir`.
    25	
    26	  (This will be passed to `lean` as the `-R` option.)
    27	  -/
    28	  srcDir : FilePath := "."
    29	
    30	  /--
    31	  The root module(s) of the library.
    32	  Submodules of these roots (e.g., `Lib.Foo` of `Lib`) are considered
    33	  part of the library.
    34	  Defaults to a single root of the target's name.
    35	  -/
    36	  roots : Array Name := #[name]
    37	
    38	  /--
    39	  An `Array` of module `Glob`s to build for the library.
    40	  Defaults to a `Glob.one` of each of the library's  `roots`.
    41	
    42	  Submodule globs build every source file within their directory.
    43	  Local imports of glob'ed files (i.e., fellow modules of the workspace) are
    44	  also recursively built.
    45	  -/
    46	  globs : Array Glob := roots.map Glob.one
    47	
    48	  /--
    49	  The name of the library artifact.
    50	  Used as a base for the file names of its static and dynamic binaries.
    51	  Defaults to the mangled name of the target.
    52	  -/
    53	  libName : String := ""
    54	
    55	  /--
    56	  Whether static and shared binaries of this library should be prefixed with `lib` on Windows.
    57	
    58	  Unlike Unix, Windows does not require native libraries to start with `lib` and,
    59	  by convention, they usually do not. However, for consistent naming across all platforms,
    60	  users may wish to enable this.
    61	
    62	  Defaults to `false`.
    63	  -/
    64	  libPrefixOnWindows : Bool := false
    65	
    66	  /-- An `Array` of targets to build before the executable's modules. -/
    67	  needs : Array PartialBuildKey := #[]
    68	
    69	  /--
    70	   **Deprecated. Use `needs` instead.**
    71	  An `Array` of target names to build before the library's modules.
    72	  -/
    73	  extraDepTargets : Array Name := #[]
    74	
    75	  /--
    76	  Whether to compile each of the library's modules into a native shared library
    77	  that is loaded whenever the module is imported. This speeds up evaluation of
    78	  metaprograms and enables the interpreter to run functions marked `@[extern]`.
    79	
    80	  Defaults to `false`.
    81	  -/
    82	  precompileModules : Bool := false
    83	
    84	  /--
    85	  An `Array` of library facets to build on a bare `lake build` of the library.
    86	  For example, `#[LeanLib.sharedFacet]` will build the shared library facet.
    87	  -/
    88	  defaultFacets : Array Name := #[LeanLib.leanArtsFacet]
    89	
    90	  /--
    91	  The module facets to build and combine into the library's static
    92	  and shared libraries. If `shouldExport` is true, the module facets should
    93	  export any symbols a user may expect to lookup in the library. For example,
    94	  the Lean interpreter will use exported symbols in linked libraries.
    95	
    96	  Defaults to a singleton of `Module.oExportFacet` (if `shouldExport`) or
    97	  `Module.oFacet`. That is, the  object files compiled from the Lean sources,
    98	  potentially with exported Lean symbols.
    99	  -/
   100	  nativeFacets (shouldExport : Bool) : Array (ModuleFacet FilePath) :=
   101	    #[if shouldExport then Module.oExportFacet else Module.oFacet]
   102	
   103	  /--
   104	  Whether downstream packages can `import all` modules of this library.
   105	
   106	  If enabled, downstream users will be able to access the `private` internals of modules,
   107	  including definition bodies not marked as `@[expose]`.
   108	  This may also, in the future, prevent compiler optimization which rely on `private`
   109	  definitions being inaccessible outside their own package.
   110	
   111	  Defaults to `false`.
   112	  -/
   113	  allowImportAll : Bool := false

   120	public abbrev name (_ : LeanLibConfig n) := n

   122	/-- Whether the given module is considered local to the library. -/
   123	public def isLocalModule (mod : Name) (self : LeanLibConfig n) : Bool :=
   124	  self.roots.any (fun root => root.isPrefixOf mod) ||
   125	  self.globs.any (fun glob => glob.matches mod)
   126	
   127	/-- Whether the given module is a buildable part of the library. -/
   128	public def isBuildableModule (mod : Name) (self : LeanLibConfig n) : Bool :=
   129	  self.globs.any (fun glob => glob.matches mod) ||
   130	  self.roots.any (fun root => root.isPrefixOf mod && self.globs.any (·.matches root))

    62	    # decidability instances needed to re-elaborate the definition body.

   283	class SplitAssembler(Assembler):

    26	/-- A finite two-player one-round game with a Mathlib probability mass function. -/
    27	structure Game (X Y A B : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Y] [Fintype A] [Fintype B]
    28	    [DecidableEq X] [DecidableEq Y] [DecidableEq A] [DecidableEq B] where
    29	  μ : PMF (X × Y)
    30	  decide : X → Y → A → B → Bool

    33	structure POVM (A I : Type*) [Fintype A] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] where

    35	  pos : ∀ a, (effect a).PosSemidef

    38	/-- A finite-dimensional pure unit-state tensor-product strategy. -/
    39	structure Strategy (X Y A B : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Y] [Fintype A] [Fintype B]

    41	  ιA : Type
    42	  ιB : Type
    43	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
    44	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]

    50	  bob : Y → POVM B ιB

    52	attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
    53	  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq

    55	/-- Reindex a finite Euclidean state along an equivalence of coordinates. -/
    56	noncomputable def reindexState {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    57	    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J] (e : I ≃ J)
    58	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ I) : EuclideanSpace ℂ J :=
    59	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv J ℂ).symm (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.equiv I ℂ ψ) (e.symm j))

    87	  bob := S.meas

--- README.md
     1	# QPBT-comparator
     2	
     3	Comparator challenge for the Lean 4 formalization of the quantum Pauli basis
     4	test in [Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A](https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A).
     5	
     6	The single comparator run checks these four registered headline declarations:
     7	
     8	- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one`;
     9	- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness`;
    10	- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness`; and
    11	- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit`.
    12	
    13	The separate Palomar preparation profile expects the final compact aliases
    14	under `MIPStarRE.QPBT.Palomar` and the definition frontier
    15	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.fixedFieldModel`. This snapshot intentionally leaves the actual
    16	`comparator.json`, split Challenge, source pin, and toolchain unchanged, so the
    17	checked-in preparation report remains red until those final inputs land.
    18	
    19	## What The Check Establishes
    20	
    21	The official [Lean comparator](https://github.com/leanprover/comparator)
    22	exports the challenge and solution environments and compares the complete
    23	statement closure declaration by declaration. A successful run establishes
    24	that the library proves exactly the four challenge statements, that every
    25	constant in their statement closures agrees, and that the proofs use no axioms
    26	beyond `propext`, `Quot.sound`, and `Classical.choice`. The workflow also
    27	replays the environment through Lean's kernel, `lean4checker`, and the
    28	independent nanoda kernel.
    29	
    30	## Layout
    31	
    32	`Challenge.lean` imports 30 generated modules below `Challenge/`, one for each
    33	contributing library module. Those 31 files import only Mathlib and other
    34	generated challenge modules. Mirroring the library module partition is
    35	necessary because compiler-generated auxiliary names and instance visibility
    36	are module-sensitive.
    37	
    38	`Solution.lean` imports the four library theorem modules. `comparator.json`
    39	names the four targets and the three permitted axioms. `lakefile.toml` and
    40	`lake-manifest.json` pin the exact library revision used to generate the
    41	challenge.
    42	
    43	## Verification
    44	
    45	On Linux with Landlock, Go, a current Rust toolchain, `jq`, and `elan`, run:
    46	
    47	```sh
    48	./verify.sh
    49	```
    50	
    51	This invokes the unchanged official comparator with real landrun and nanoda.
    52	For diagnostics only, `./verify.sh --fake-landrun` substitutes the comparator's
    53	development sandbox and disables nanoda; that mode is not official acceptance.
    54	
    55	The authoritative GitHub workflow checks the Mathlib-only import boundary,
    56	the full revision pin, Lean compilation and kernel replay, then runs the real

     4	# lakefile.toml and lake-manifest.json) proves exactly the statements in
     5	# Challenge.lean using only propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice, replayed

     7	# is Challenge.lean together with the modules under Challenge/.  See the
     8	# Validating Proofs chapter of the Lean reference manual for the trust model.
     9	#
    10	# The systemd-run guard from the comparator README is omitted: it hardens
    11	# against landrun escapes by untrusted solutions, and both modules here come
    12	# from this trusted checkout.
    13	#
    14	# This is the authoritative run.  On the development host the sandbox and the
    15	# external kernel are unavailable (no Go, no modern Rust), so local runs use
    16	# ./verify.sh --fake-landrun and are functional checks only.

    18	on:

    21	  pull_request:
    22	  workflow_dispatch:
    23	  schedule:

    38	      - name: Check the challenge imports only Mathlib and its own modules

    42	          # Challenge modules, and nothing else -- in particular never the

    44	          files="Challenge.lean $(find Challenge -name '*.lean' | sort)"

    46	                | grep -vE '^import Mathlib$|^import Challenge(\.[A-Za-z0-9_.]+)?$' \

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""Load and validate Palomar's published verification resource policy."""
     3	
     4	from __future__ import annotations
     5	
     6	import hashlib
     7	import json

    10	import re
    11	import shutil
    12	from pathlib import Path
    13	from typing import Any
    14	
    15	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    16	PROFILE_PATH = ROOT / "verification-profile.json"
    17	CATALOGUE_PATH = ROOT / "execution-profiles.json"
    18	
    19	
    20	class VerificationProfileError(RuntimeError):
    21	    pass
    22	
    23	
    24	HOSTED_PROFILE = "palomar-standard-v1"
    25	NAMESPACE_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r"^nscloud-ubuntu-24\.04-amd64-\d+x\d+-with-features$")
    26	NAMESPACE_FEATURE_LABEL = "namespace-features:container.privileged=true"
    27	CATALOGUE_LIMITS = {"minimum_host_memory_bytes", "job_timeout_minutes", "execution_budget_seconds"}
    28	
    29	
    30	def load_catalogue() -> dict[str, Any]:
    31	    """The approved execution profiles beside the hosted one, validated by shape."""
    32	    catalogue = json.loads(CATALOGUE_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    33	    if (
    34	        not isinstance(catalogue, dict)
    35	        or catalogue.get("schema_version") != 1
    36	        or not isinstance(catalogue.get("default"), str)
    37	        or not isinstance(catalogue.get("profiles"), dict)
    38	    ):
    39	        raise VerificationProfileError("approved execution profile catalogue is malformed")
    40	    for identifier, selected in catalogue["profiles"].items():
    41	        if not re.fullmatch(r"palomar-[a-z0-9-]+-v\d+", identifier) or identifier == HOSTED_PROFILE:
    42	            raise VerificationProfileError(f"execution profile id is malformed: {identifier}")
    43	        runner = selected.get("runner") if isinstance(selected, dict) else None
    44	        limits = selected.get("limits") if isinstance(selected, dict) else None
    45	        if (
    46	            set(selected) != {"runner", "limits"}
    47	            or not isinstance(runner, dict)
    48	            or set(runner) != {"provider", "label", "labels", "architecture"}
    49	            or runner["provider"] != "namespace"
    50	            or runner["architecture"] != "x86_64"
    51	            or not NAMESPACE_LABEL_RE.fullmatch(str(runner["label"]))
    52	            or runner["labels"] != [runner["label"], NAMESPACE_FEATURE_LABEL]
    53	            or not isinstance(limits, dict)
    54	            or set(limits) != CATALOGUE_LIMITS
    55	            or any(type(limits[name]) is not int or limits[name] <= 0 for name in CATALOGUE_LIMITS)
    56	            or limits["execution_budget_seconds"] > limits["job_timeout_minutes"] * 60
    57	        ):
    58	            raise VerificationProfileError(f"approved execution profile is malformed: {identifier}")
    59	    if catalogue["default"] != HOSTED_PROFILE and catalogue["default"] not in catalogue["profiles"]:
    60	        raise VerificationProfileError("approved execution profile catalogue default is not approved")
    61	    return catalogue
    62	
    63	
    64	def default_profile_id() -> str:
    65	    return load_catalogue()["default"]
    66	
    67	
    68	def load_profile(identifier: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    69	    identifier = identifier or os.environ.get("PALOMAR_EXECUTION_PROFILE") or default_profile_id()
    70	    value = json.loads(PROFILE_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    71	    if not isinstance(value, dict) or set(value) != {
    72	        "schema_version",
    73	        "id",
    74	        "runner",
    75	        "limits",
    76	        "trusted_tools",
    77	        "cache_policy",
    78	    }:
    79	        raise VerificationProfileError("verification profile has an invalid top-level shape")
    80	    if value["schema_version"] != 1 or value["id"] != "palomar-standard-v1":
    81	        raise VerificationProfileError("verification profile identity is unsupported")
    82	    runner = value["runner"]
    83	    if not isinstance(runner, dict) or set(runner) != {"provider", "label", "architecture"}:
    84	        raise VerificationProfileError("verification profile runner is invalid")
    85	    limits = value["limits"]
    86	    expected_limits = {
    87	        "job_timeout_minutes",
    88	        "execution_budget_seconds",
    89	        "memory_high_percent",
    90	        "memory_max_percent",
    91	        "minimum_workspace_free_bytes",
    92	        "tasks_max",
    93	        "open_files_max",
    94	        "file_size_max_bytes",
    95	        "minimum_host_memory_bytes",
    96	    }
    97	    if not isinstance(limits, dict) or set(limits) != expected_limits:
    98	        raise VerificationProfileError("verification profile limits are invalid")
    99	    if any(type(limits[name]) is not int or limits[name] <= 0 for name in expected_limits):
   100	        raise VerificationProfileError("verification profile limits must be positive integers")
   101	    if not (limits["memory_high_percent"] < limits["memory_max_percent"] <= 100):
   102	        raise VerificationProfileError("memory_high_percent must be below memory_max_percent")
   103	    if limits["execution_budget_seconds"] > limits["job_timeout_minutes"] * 60:
   104	        raise VerificationProfileError("execution budget exceeds the job timeout")
   105	    # What judges a submission is the submitted toolchain itself (at or above
   106	    # the floor) and the bubblewrap release the trusted phase builds; the
   107	    # profile names both so the record's provenance and the policy agree.
   108	    tools = value["trusted_tools"]
   109	    expected_tools = {"toolchain_floor", "bwrap_source_tag"}
   110	    if not isinstance(tools, dict) or set(tools) != expected_tools:
   111	        raise VerificationProfileError("verification profile trusted tools are invalid")
   112	    if not all(isinstance(tools[name], str) for name in expected_tools):
   113	        raise VerificationProfileError("verification profile trusted tools must be strings")
   114	    if not re.fullmatch(r"v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(?:-rc[0-9]+)?", tools["toolchain_floor"]):
   115	        raise VerificationProfileError("verification profile toolchain_floor is not a release tag")
   116	    if not re.fullmatch(r"v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+", tools["bwrap_source_tag"]):
   117	        raise VerificationProfileError("verification profile bwrap_source_tag is not a release tag")
   118	    if identifier != HOSTED_PROFILE:
   119	        catalogue = load_catalogue()
   120	        selected = catalogue["profiles"].get(identifier)
   121	        if not isinstance(selected, dict):
   122	            raise VerificationProfileError("execution profile is not approved")
   123	        value["id"] = identifier
   124	        value["runner"] = selected["runner"]
   125	        value["limits"].update(selected["limits"])
   126	    return value

   129	def profile_digest(profile: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
   130	    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(profile, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()).hexdigest()
   131	
   132	
   133	def cgroup_directories() -> list[Path]:
   134	    """The process's cgroup-v2 ancestors, including a namespaced mount root."""
   135	    root = Path("/sys/fs/cgroup")
   136	    try:
   137	        relative = next(
   138	            line[3:] for line in Path("/proc/self/cgroup").read_text().splitlines() if line.startswith("0::")
   139	        )
   140	        if ".." in Path(relative).parts:
   141	            return [root]
   142	        leaf = root / relative.lstrip("/")
   143	        return [leaf, *[parent for parent in leaf.parents if parent == root or root in parent.parents]]
   144	    except (OSError, StopIteration):
   145	        return [root]
   146	
   147	
   148	def effective_memory_bytes() -> int:
   149	    limits = [host_memory_bytes()]
   150	    for directory in cgroup_directories():
   151	        try:
   152	            raw = (directory / "memory.max").read_text().strip()
   153	            if raw.isdigit():
   154	                limits.append(int(raw))
   155	        except OSError:
   156	            continue
   157	    return min(limits)
   158	
   159	
   160	def effective_cpu_count() -> float:
   161	    cpus = float(len(os.sched_getaffinity(0)))
   162	    for directory in cgroup_directories():
   163	        try:
   164	            quota, period = (directory / "cpu.max").read_text().split()
   165	            if quota.isdigit() and int(period) > 0:
   166	                cpus = min(cpus, int(quota) / int(period))
   167	        except (OSError, ValueError):
   168	            continue
   169	    return cpus
   170	
   171	
   172	def host_memory_bytes() -> int:
   173	    for line in Path("/proc/meminfo").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
   174	        if line.startswith("MemTotal:"):
   175	            return int(line.split()[1]) * 1024
   176	    raise VerificationProfileError("could not read host memory capacity")
   177	
   178	
   179	def check_host(profile: dict[str, Any], disk_path: Path) -> dict[str, int | float | str]:
   180	    runner = profile["runner"]
   181	    limits = profile["limits"]
   182	    architecture = platform.machine()
   183	    accepted_architectures = {"x86_64": {"x86_64", "amd64"}}
   184	    if architecture.lower() not in accepted_architectures.get(runner["architecture"], set()):
   185	        raise VerificationProfileError(
   186	            f"runner architecture {architecture!r} does not satisfy {runner['architecture']}"
   187	        )
   188	    cpus = effective_cpu_count()
   189	    if profile["id"] == "palomar-namespace-16x32-v1" and cpus < 16:
   190	        raise VerificationProfileError(f"runner has {cpus} effective CPUs; Namespace profile requires 16")
   191	    memory = effective_memory_bytes()
   192	    if memory < limits["minimum_host_memory_bytes"]:
   193	        raise VerificationProfileError(
   194	            f"runner has {memory} memory bytes; profile requires {limits['minimum_host_memory_bytes']}"
   195	        )
   196	    workspace = shutil.disk_usage(disk_path).free
   197	    if workspace < limits["minimum_workspace_free_bytes"]:
   198	        raise VerificationProfileError(
   199	            f"runner has {workspace} free workspace bytes; profile requires "
   200	            f"{limits['minimum_workspace_free_bytes']}"
   201	        )
   202	    return {
   203	        "architecture": architecture,
   204	        "effective_cpus": cpus,
   205	        "memory_bytes": memory,
   206	        "workspace_free_bytes": workspace,
   207	        "memory_high_bytes": memory * limits["memory_high_percent"] // 100,
   208	        "memory_max_bytes": memory * limits["memory_max_percent"] // 100,
   209	    }
   210	
   211	
   212	def main() -> int:
   213	    import argparse
   214	
   215	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
   216	    parser.add_argument("--disk-path", type=Path)
   217	    parser.add_argument("--profile", default=None)
   218	    parser.add_argument("--resolve", action="store_true")
   219	    args = parser.parse_args()
   220	    profile = load_profile(args.profile)
   221	    if args.resolve:
   222	        runner = profile["runner"]
   223	        labels = runner.get("labels", [runner["label"]])
   224	        outputs = {
   225	            "labels": json.dumps(labels),

   227	            "digest": profile_digest(profile),

   230	            # budget already bounds; it gets the verification timeout plus a

   243	    return 0

   211	def resolve_release_commit(repository: str, tag: str) -> str:
   212	    """The commit a tooling release points at.
   213	
   214	    The tag is resolved once and the commit it named is recorded in the
   215	    mechanical report, so a record always says exactly which revision of
   216	    Palomar's own tooling checked it, whatever the tag says afterwards.
   217	    """
   218	    proc = subprocess.run(
   219	        ["git", "ls-remote", f"https://github.com/{repository}", f"refs/tags/{tag}^{{}}",
   220	         f"refs/tags/{tag}"],
   221	        check=False,
   222	        capture_output=True,
   223	        text=True,
   224	        timeout=120,
   225	    )
   226	    if proc.returncode != 0:
   227	        raise VerificationError(
   228	            f"could not read {repository} releases",
   229	            code="provider.release_lookup_failed",
   230	            owner="provider",
   231	            next_action="Do not change the repository. Retry the same commit later.",
   232	            retryable=True,
   233	        )
   234	    commits = {}
   235	    for line in proc.stdout.splitlines():
   236	        parts = line.split()
   237	        if len(parts) == 2 and submission_contract.SHA_RE.fullmatch(parts[0]):
   238	            commits[parts[1]] = parts[0]
   239	    # An annotated tag resolves through its peeled ref; prefer that.
   240	    commit = commits.get(f"refs/tags/{tag}^{{}}") or commits.get(f"refs/tags/{tag}")
   241	    if not commit:
   242	        raise VerificationError(
   243	            f"{repository} has published no {tag} release",
   244	            code="palomar.toolchain_release_missing",
   245	            owner="palomar",
   246	            next_action=(
   247	                "Do not change the repository. Palomar must add support for this Lean release."
   248	            ),
   249	        )
   250	    return commit

   455	        elapsed = max(0.0, _WALL_TIME() - started_at)

   471	def _bounded_stream_reader(stream: Any, destination: bytearray) -> None:
   472	    omitted = 0
   473	    try:
   474	        while True:
   475	            chunk = stream.read(64 * 1024)
   476	            if not chunk:
   477	                break
   478	            destination.extend(chunk)
   479	            if len(destination) > MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES:
   480	                excess = len(destination) - MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES
   481	                del destination[:excess]
   482	                omitted += excess
   483	    finally:
   484	        stream.close()
   485	    if omitted:
   486	        marker = f"<output truncated; omitted {omitted} bytes>\n".encode()
   487	        destination[:0] = marker
